correctness.rationale: The proof partitions every monotone map \(P_{p,q}\to\mathfrak C_n\) into four exhaustive image-shape cases, derives the exact count in each case, and exhibits a pointwise comparable constant map. The only nontrivial local lemma is the common-neighbor property of the crown for \(n\ge3\), which follows immediately because each target maximum covers exactly two consecutive minima and two distinct minima have at most one common upper neighbor. The independent script exhaustively confirms the formula and witnesses on \(27\) small parameter triples and verifies the sharp \(n=2\) boundary. The computation is explicitly not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The claim completely solves a natural mapping problem between two basic graph-model families: it gives an exact closed count and shows that all direct maps collapse to one finite-space homotopy class for every \(p,q\ge2\), \(n\ge3\). The source order complex has cycle rank \((p-1)(q-1)\) and the target models a circle, so the all-null result exposes a genuine direct-representability obstruction rather than a trivial contractibility phenomenon. The explicit failure at \(n=2\) makes the threshold mathematically sharp.
